info.description:
This API provides endpoints for defining, modifying and accessing customer-specific business resources. The Asset Management API supports adding arbitrary number of fields and widgets to these and also supports defining basic relationship rules between them. The term 'asset' represents any business resource in the broader sense. They are grouped into 'categories' - by the 'resourceCategory' property - based on their major traits, which may differ substantially for tangible entities and abstract resource definitions. Resource categories define rules, introduce restrictions, but they also provide access to additional APIs specific for them. Basically all Asset Management endpoints can be used for all resource categories, taking the pre-defined restrictions into consideration. Currently the following resource categories are supported:
  • asset - The default resource category for representing identifiable entities.
  • bulkItem - Represents items that are not valuable enough to track them individually.
  • stock - A stock, in the common sense, to which assets and bulk items can be linked. There is a pre-defined link type which represents that an asset is in stock, and another one which represents that a bulk item is in stock. Check the 'Asset links' section about how to put/remove assets into/from stocks. Check the 'Stock Quantities' section to find out how to add/remove a specific amount of bulk items to/from stocks.
info.title: Asset Management REST API

tags.description:
Business resources can be linked together using 'link types'. Pre-defined link types are available, but new ones can be defined by users.
  • assets in stocks - A pre-defined link type which represents that an asset is in stock. It's only valid between stocks as source and assets as target and an asset can be linked to at most one stock at a time. Its capabilityId is DAD98DAD-054B-41AE-A727-3E3B37342739 which can be used for linking assets to stocks through the normal API endpoints. It can also be used in other endpoints where a capabilityId is expected, for example to list all assets on a specific stock:
    GET /assets?linkedToAsset={stockId}&linkedWithDirection=source&linkedWithCapability=DAD98DAD-054B-41AE-A727-3E3B37342739
  • bulk items in stocks - A pre-defined link type which represents that a bulk item is in stock. It's only valid between stocks as source and bulk items as target. Its capabilityId is 7777BAE8-7EA5-4F82-A1C1-49E54DD3b6A7. It can be used in endpoints where a capabilityId is expected, for example to list all bulk items on a specific stock:
    GET /assets?linkedToAsset={stockId}&linkedWithDirection=source&linkedWithCapability=7777BAE8-7EA5-4F82-A1C1-49E54DD3b6A7&resourceCategory=bulkItem
    This type of link is not allowed to be created with POST /assetLinks or to be removed with DELETE /assetLinks/{relationId}. See endpoints in the 'Stock Quantities' section to find out how to perform these two operations.

get.description:
Returns a list of assets. By default the following fields are included: id, name (text), etag and state (archived). You can use various parameters to filter this list or to retrieve other fields from the assets.

Branch filters are applied to the assets, as well as to their (person, person group, branch, location) assignments in the response.

⚠️**Deprecation warning**: the `application/x.topdesk-am-assets-v1+json` media type is deprecated and is going to be removed in a future release. As a consequence, the "type" and the "icon" property of objects in the "dataSet" array won't be included in the response unless requested. Currently, their value is the name and the icon of the template, respectively. We strongly recommend setting the Accept header of each request to `application/x.topdesk-am-assets-v2+json` in order to get the new version of the assets resource and to follow the best practice of depending on a specific resource version explicitly. With the new version, the value of the "type" and the "icon" property changes to the value of the corresponding user-defined fields, if they exist, otherwise it changes to "null". To retrieve the name or the icon of the template, read the "name" and the "icon" properties of the "@type" object within "dataSet" items, respectively.

Timeline:
- After the end of April, 2024, support for the `application/x.topdesk-am-assets-v1+json` media type is going to be dropped entirely.

parameters.description:
Specifies the set of returned asset fields and auxiliary asset information. Field names are to be provided as a comma-separated list of the same query parameter. The specified pieces of information are returned inside the 'dataSet' array. Additional meta-data about the requested fields (like their type and display name) is returned in the 'columns' array of the response. Possible values are the following:
  • The ID of any user-defined field can be used.
  • Standard asset properties: 'name', 'modificationDate', 'creationDate'.
  • '@type': Template name and icon name of the asset.
  • '@@summary': a user-defined description of the asset which is built by concatenating field values.
  • '@assignments': Information about assignments (person / person group / location / branch links) of the particular asset.
  • '@linkToTemplateCount': This field can only be used together with 'linkedToTemplate', 'linkedToTemplateWithDirection', and optionally with 'linkedToTemplateWithCapability' query parameters. When this special field is given, the response will contain the count of assets of the specified template which are linked to the given asset with the specified direction and capability. If 'linkedToTemplateWithCapability' isn't given, the unqualified parent-child relationship is assumed. (For example, this feature can be used to query how many assets of a certain asset type are in each stock.)
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description:
Entity type and ID of the entity the assets are linked to, separated by a slash character. Accepted types: assignable types (person, personGroup, branch, location) and external link types (incident, changeActivity, knowledge, change, problem, omActivity, omSeries, service).
- Example: `linkedTo=person/4878f620-e404-4f2d-9d53-622a1693d467`.
- Instead of an ID, wildcards can also be used with certain types.  In that case, and only then, multiple type/value pairs are also accepted, which should be separated by a comma.
  * Supported wildcards are:
    - 'any' for any active or archived entities. Supported for the following types: person, personGroup, branch, location, service.
    - 'anyArchived' for any archived entities. Supported for the following types: person, personGroup.
  * Example: `linkedTo=person/any,personGroup/anyArchived`.    This filters for assets that are linked to any person or linked to any archived person group.
- At most one type/value pair can be specified when the type is an external link type, and   it cannot be combined with assignable types.
parameters.name: linkedTo

parameters.description:
Entity type and ID of the entity the assets are *not* linked to, separated by a slash character. Accepted types are the same as for linkedTo.
- Example: `notLinkedTo=person/4878f620-e404-4f2d-9d53-622a1693d467`.
- Instead of an ID, wildcards can also be used with certain types.  In that case, and only then, multiple type/value pairs are also accepted, which should be separated by a comma.
  * Supported wildcards are:
    - 'any' for any active or archived entities. Supported for the following types: person, personGroup, branch, location.
    - 'anyArchived' for any archived entities. Supported for the following types: person, personGroup.
  * Example: `notLinkedTo=person/any,personGroup/anyArchived`. This filters for assets that are     not linked to any person or not linked to any archived person group.
- At most one type/value pair can be specified when the type is an external link type, and   it cannot be combined with assignable types.
parameters.name: notLinkedTo

parameters.description:
Used together with linkedTo or notLinkedTo parameters. Whether to filter assets by including inherited assignments. For example:
  • Using filterInherited=false and linkedTo=person/4878f620-e404-4f2d-9d53-622a1693d467 lists all assets which have this person assigned directly, but skips assets where this person is assigned only by inheritance.
  • Using filterInherited=true and linkedTo=person/4878f620-e404-4f2d-9d53-622a1693d467 lists all assets which have this person assigned, either directly or by inheritance.
parameters.name: filterInherited

parameters.description:
Supports a set of OData filters which can be combined with 'and' and 'or' operators. Filter expressions can also be grouped by parentheses.
- Filtering based on the name field with greater-than operator. Example: `$filter=name gt 'CAR0042'`.
- Filtering based on the templateId field. Supported operators: eq, in, ne. Example: `$filter=templateId eq 'fc886aa0-8315-4ff9-b7f9-ad79a01d5f5c' and templateId eq '3c5f3383-23d5-40bf-95f0-78b151c028ea'`.
- Filtering based on the ID of the reason for archiving. Supported operators: eq, in. Example: `$filter=archiveReason in ['add003d1-d7e1-4776-8d1d-ebc79864fc68', 'e5437db1-0ea9-412b-948f-c38f5b2ce425']`.
- Filtering based on date fields with greater-than, less-than, greater-than-or-equals, less-than-or-equals, equals, and non-equals operators. Example: `$filter=modificationDate gt '2017' and modificationDate lt '2017-05-26'`.
  * Dates are interpreted as UTC dates.
  * Supported formats: yyyy (2017); yyyy-MM (2017-12); yyyy-MM-dd (2017-12-25); yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm (2017-12-25T18:30); yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss (2017-12-25T18:30:12); yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS (2017-12-25T18:30:12.798). When hours, minutes or seconds are omitted, they are considered to be 0. When month is omitted it's considered to be January.  When day is omitted, it's considered to be '1'.
  * The following relative date ranges are also supported with `eq` and `ne` operator: `lastYear`, `thisYear`, `nextYear`, `lastMonth`, `thisMonth`, `nextMonth`, `lastWeek`, `thisWeek`, `nextWeek`, `yesterday`, `today`, `tomorrow`. These intervals are meant to be in the server's current time and time zone. First day of the week is considered to be 'Sunday'.
- Filtering based on a linked entity. Example: `$filter=linkedTo eq 'incident/2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b06'`. Note, that this filter can be also expressed by the more flexible 'isLinkedTo' function. Possible external link types are: incident, changeActivity, knowledge, change, problem, omActivity, omSeries, service. Currently external link types other than 'service' are not supported when combining filters with the ‘or’ operator, or as part of nested filters.
- Filtering based on linked assets: `isLinkedTo(<asset or stock ID>, <capability ID>, <direction>)`. For the meaning and usage of the three function arguments check `linkedToAsset`, `linkedWithCapability`, and `linkedWithDirection` query parameters. The function must have three arguments but `<capability ID>` can be null. Examples:
  * Assets that are linked to a specific asset with a specific link type and direction (source): `isLinkedTo('e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'source')`
  * Assets that are linked to a specific asset with a specific link type and direction (target): `isLinkedTo('e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'target')`
  * Assets that are linked to the given assets either as source or target: `isLinkedTo('e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'any')`
  * Assets that are not linked to the given asset as source neither as target: `isLinkedTo('e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'none')`
  * Assets that are linked to any asset with a specific link type and direction: `isLinkedTo('any', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'source')`
  * Assets that are not linked to any asset with a specific link type and direction: `isLinkedTo('none', '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b44', 'source')`
  * If `<capability ID>` is null, it means the default parent/child relationship: `isLinkedTo('e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727', null, 'source')`
- Filtering based on linked external entities are also supported by the `isLinkedTo()` function where the meaning of the parameters are the following: `isLinkedTo(<external entity ID or wildcard>, <capability ID>, <direction>)`.
  * For external entities `<capability ID>` is always null and `<direction>` is always 'source' or 'none'.
  * External entity ID's format: `service/2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b06`.
  * Wildcards are supported only for 'services': `isLinkedTo('service/any', null, 'source')`,`isLinkedTo('service/none', null, 'source')`
  * Assets which are not linked to a specific service can be expressed like this: `isLinkedTo('service/2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b06', null, 'none')`
- Filtering based on a text field. Use the 'contains' operator. Example: `$filter=specification contains 'desk'`.
- Filtering based on a checkbox field on false and true values. Example: `$filter=termsandconditions eq 'false'`.
- Filtering based on a number field. Examples: `$filter=cost eq 15`, `$filter=cost ge 40`.
- Filtering based on a dropdown field. Supported operators: eq, in, ne. Example: `$filter=dropdown-field eq '2eebf650-c5d7-4bf3-ad05-1f4cbced3b06'`.
- Filtering based on whether a text, number, dropdown or date field is empty or not empty. Missing values and empty strings are considered empty. Fields that do not exist for a given type are considered neither empty nor not empty. Examples: `$filter=text-field isEmpty`, `$filter=text-field isNotEmpty`.
- Filtering based on the id field with 'eq' or 'in' operator. Examples: `$filter=id eq 'e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727'`, `$filter=id in ['e08dcc19-8008-436e-82f1-c99b1cf9d727','23c484cd-cdcf-48ae-a7bd-b655efb3c686']`. Combining this kind of filter with others using the ‘or’ operator, or creating nested filters of it are not supported.
parameters.name: $filter

parameters.description: OData like ordering on assets based on the value of a *single field* specified by this parameter. Secondary ordering is always performed by name. Sorting direction needs to be set to either *asc* or *desc*. Currently, sorting can be based on the following types of fields: text (including name and @@summary), date (including modificationDate and creationDate), number, boolean, and dropdown with own options.
parameters.name: $orderby

parameters.description:
Can be used for implementing seek-based paging. Skips assets whose name precedes or equals to the value of this parameter according to the sorting direction. Can be used together with *lastSeenOrderbyValue* and *$orderby*. If *lastSeenOrderbyValue* is not present, using this parameter leads to a bad request error.

Note: Using this parameter is only supported when *$orderby* is set to either name, @@summary, modificationDate, or creationDate.
parameters.name: lastSeenName

parameters.description:
Can be used for implementing seek-based paging. Skips assets that have a preceding value for the field specified in *$orderby* compared to the value of this parameter. In case of value equality the value of *lastSeenName* determines whether to skip an asset or not. Can be used together with *lastSeenName* and *$orderby*. When sorting is based on the name only, the value of this parameter should be the same as the value of *lastSeenName*. If *lastSeenName* is not present, using this parameter leads to a bad request error.

Note: Using this parameter is only supported when *$orderby* is set to either name, @@summary, modificationDate, or creationDate.
parameters.name: lastSeenOrderbyValue

parameters.description: Used together with *linkableWithDirection* and optionally with *linkableWithCapability*. To filter assets by checking if they can be linked to the asset specified by its unique ID. An asset cannot be linked to itself. The same link cannot be applied multiple times. If *linkableWithDirection* is not provided, using this parameter results in a 'Bad Request' error. If *linkableWithCapability* is not provided, resulting assets are linkable without a link type.
parameters.name: linkableToAsset

parameters.description:
Used together with *linkableToAsset* and optionally with *linkableWithCapability*. To filter assets by direction. Possible values: SOURCE, TARGET.

SOURCE: *linkableToAsset* can be the parent of results.

TARGET: *linkableToAsset* can be the child of results.

If *linkableToAsset* is not provided, using this parameter  results in a 'Bad Request' error. If *linkableWithCapability* is not provided, resulting assets are linkable without a link type.
parameters.name: linkableWithDirection

parameters.description: Used together with *linkableWithDirection* and *linkableToAsset*. To filter assets by a link type specified by its unique ID. If either *linkableWithDirection* or *linkableToAsset* is not provided, using this parameter results in a 'Bad Request' error.
parameters.name: linkableWithCapability

parameters.description:
Used together with *linkedWithDirection* and optionally with *linkedWithCapability*. To filter assets by checking if they are linked to the asset specified by its unique ID. If *linkedWithDirection* is not provided, using this parameter results in a 'Bad Request' error. If *linkedWithCapability* is not provided, resulting assets are linked without a link type. In addition to a unique ID of an asset, the following values are also valid for the parameter:
- any: results in assets that are linked to any asset with the specified direction and link type.
- none: results in assets that are not linked to any asset with the specified direction and link type. This value is supported for backward compatibility reasons, as the same effect can be achieved by using *linkedWithDirection=none* in combination with *linkedToAsset=any*. Setting both *linkedWithDirection* and *linkedToAsset* to *none* results in a 'Bad Request' error.
parameters.name: linkedToAsset

parameters.description:
Used together with *linkedToAsset* and optionally with *linkedWithCapability*. To filter assets by direction. Possible, case-insensitive values:
- source: *linkedToAsset* can be the parent of results.
- target: *linkedToAsset* can be the child of results.
- any: *linkedToAsset* can be either the parent or the child of results.
- none: *linkedToAsset* is not linked to the resulting assets.

If *linkedToAsset* is not provided, using this parameter results in a 'Bad Request' error. If *linkedWithCapability* is not provided, resulting assets are linked without a link type.
parameters.name: linkedWithDirection

parameters.description: Used together with *linkedWithDirection* and *linkedToAsset*. To filter assets by a link type specified by its unique ID. When left unspecified, the absence of a custom link type is assumed. In addition to a unique ID of a link type, 'any' is also a valid value. 'any' indicates that all link types match, including relationships without a link type. If either *linkedWithDirection* or *linkedToAsset* is not provided, using this parameter results in a 'Bad Request' error.
parameters.name: linkedWithCapability

put.description:
Assigns assets, stocks and bulk items with proper type of cards.
  • Assets can be assigned to locations, branches, persons and person groups
  • Stocks can be assigned to a single branch or location
  • Bulk items can be assigned to a branches or locations
Bulk linking of multiple assets, stocks and bulk items to a single card is supported within one request. The maximum number of assets/stocks/bulk items to be handled within a single request is 50. The type of the assignment (linkType) and the ID of the card to be assigned is required to assign a card to the asset, stock or bulk item.

requestBody.description: assetIds is an asset, stock or bulk item ID array. Multiple values of the array is supported linkType is the type of the target card - branch, location for assets, stocks and bulk items while person, personGroup is only for assets linkToId is the ID of the target card branchId (optional) - is the parent branch ID of the location.

400.description:
Possible causes:
  • Assigning person or person group to stocks or bulk items is not allowed.
  • Asset ID array has constraints: there aren't any asset IDs defined or the size of the asset IDs array exceeds the limit of 50 items.
  • There is an asset ID duplication.
  • One of the assets, stocks or bulk items is archived or not found.
  • Location, branch, person or person group to be assigned is not found.
  • When the assignment is archived.

403.description:
Possible causes:
  • When the user doesn't have permission for the operation.

409.description: One of the assets, stocks or bulk items is already assigned with the target card.

put.summary: Add branch, location, person and person group assignments to assets, stocks or bulk items.

    "608a1fa9-91e0-423a-9c0b-ad32fe6961e9"

}
